newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips extend rebound, secondaries surge.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips extend rebound, secondaries surge.

text.p: Buyers continued to filter back into the Kuala Lumpur share market on Tuesday, lifting blue chips moderately and sending small-capitalisation counters sharply higher in subdued trading.

"The Second Board's up on a rebound," said an institutional dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm. He added that gains were also seen in a "handful of index-linked stocks", but added, "none are exciting."
Building on session gains, the Composite Index closed up 11.22 points or 0.93 percent to 1,214.58, while the Second Board jumped 27.83 points or 5.20 percent to 562.77.
Despite the impressive rise in the Second Board, most dealers said business was paltry and interest thin, with many investors on holiday or wrapped up for the year.
"The beach, the sun, the waves look more appealing than the market," said Tony Shue, a vice president in institutional sales at Jupiter Securities.
Said another dealer, "We understand the Japanese have been buying, but today we've been relatively quiet. I think some people are already winding down (for the year)."
At the close, just over 188 million shares changed hands, with 54 million from the Second Board.
